problem: If the $16$th term of an arithmetic series is $-32$ and the sum of the first $20$ terms is $-200,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
We are given one term of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=20$ and ${S}_{N}=-200$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ -200 & =\frac{20}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(20-1)d) \\ -200 & =10(2{a}_{1}+19d) \\ -20 & =2{a}_{1}+19d.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we can write an equation for the $16$th term of the arithmetic series and substitute in its known value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ {a}_{16} & ={a}_{1}+(16-1)d \\ -32 & ={a}_{1}+15d\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-32={a}_{1}+15d \\ -20=2{a}_{1}+19d\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and add the result to the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}64 & =-2{a}_{1}-30d \\ -20 & =2{a}_{1}+19d \\ 44 & =-11d \\ d & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $d=-4$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-32 & ={a}_{1}+15d \\ -32 & ={a}_{1}+15(-4) \\ -32 & ={a}_{1}-60 \\ {a}_{1} & =28.\end{aligned}
$$
